title: Shared definitions for risk-compliance-core skill schemas
description: Shared $defs that per-skill schemas in this plugin commonly redefine. Per-skill schemas should $ref these via "../_defs.json#/$defs/<name>" rather than redefining the same enums and shapes inline. Stable contract: additive changes only between minor versions; breaking changes ship as a versioned migration. severity_enum uses {low, medium, high, critical}; the issue.schema.json severity ladder uses {low, moderate, high, critical} and stays inline because the moderate level has settled jurisprudence in audit findings and exam letters that the four-step low/medium/high/critical scale loses.

severity_enum.description: Standard four-step severity ladder for risks, findings, control gaps, residual exposures, and similar ratings. Always paired with a free-text rationale field on the consuming object; severity assignment carries human review.

severity_enum_with_moderate.description: Variant ladder used by issue write-ups, audit findings, exam-letter ingestion, and any artifact where 'moderate' has settled meaning in the source taxonomy. Use this where the source guidance or firm policy uses 'moderate'; otherwise use severity_enum.

confidence_label.description: Author confidence in the artifact as a whole. Reflects source posture, evidence depth, and how settled the underlying analysis is. 'unknown' is used when the artifact cannot yet be calibrated.

owner_role.description: Named firm function or role with accountability (e.g., 'Head of Model Risk', 'Chief Compliance Officer', 'Head of TPRM', 'CRO', 'BSA Officer', 'Chief Privacy Officer', 'Head of Vendor Management'). Never an individual person. Generic team labels (e.g., 'Risk team', 'Compliance') are insufficient. Where the role taxonomy is firm-specific, the value comes from references/firm-overlay.md.

claim.description: The specific claim or assertion being grounded.

source.description: Document, system, person, intake field, named regulatory citation, or '[evidence needed]' when the source is not yet anchored.

evidence_pointer.description: Pointer back to the underlying evidence: file path, system-of-record record ID, source-anchors entry, sample report ID, or path into references/source-anchors.md.

confidence.description: Per-claim confidence. 'evidence-needed' means the claim is provisional and a human reviewer must anchor the source before sign-off.

source_trace_entry.description: Single row of an artifact's source trace. The source trace is the artifact's evidence ledger; downstream reviewers and regulators read it before they read the body.

gate_name.description: Operational-language name for the gate (e.g., 'Severity sign-off gate', 'Pre-filing legal review gate', 'Tier-1 use-case go-live gate'). Names that read as slogans fail the namespace test.

criterion.description: Declarative criterion the gate enforces (e.g., 'severity rating attested by named role', 'no open critical issues against the artifact', 'independent reviewer has signed off').

required_reviewer_role.description: Role required to attest at the gate. Independence requirement is set by the consuming schema where source guidance demands it (SR 11-7, Interagency TPRM, EU AI Act Article 14).

stop_condition.description: Declarative, binary blocker. 'Should be reviewed' is not a stop condition. The stop condition is what halts the artifact's downstream use if the gate fails.

evidence_required.description: What gets captured at the gate (decision, rationale, named attesters, date, artifact references, system of record). 'Noted' is not evidence; the evidence is the artifact.

downstream_action.description: What happens after a pass (artifact is filed, escalated, published, consumed by next skill). What happens after a no-pass (escalation path, remediation route).

human_review_gate.description: Embedded human-review-gate descriptor. The full gate matrix lives in human-review-gates/schemas/review-gate-matrix.schema.json; this shape is the per-artifact reference any skill can carry without pulling the whole matrix.

engagement_id.description: Foreign key into engagement-scope.schema.json. Empty string acceptable when supplied is false.

supplied.description: True when the artifact was produced under a formal engagement scope. False when the artifact was produced ad-hoc; downstream consumers treat unsupplied work product as draft until an engagement scope is attached.

engagement_scope_ref.description: Pointer into engagement-scoping. Carrying the supplied flag explicitly is more useful than an absent field; reviewers know the artifact's provenance posture at a glance.
